extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, Marketplace/Exchange administrators, agents/brokers, and policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts regulatory standards and operational guidance governing Federally-facilitated Marketplace (FFM) and QHP issuer actions on terminations for nonpayment, grace periods, notices, special enrollment verification, APTC treatment, and related Marketplace procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on terminating newly-selected same QHP for prior unpaid premium
rubrics_metrics.description: If the [qualified individual] selects the same QHP from which he or she was previously terminated [for non-payment of premiums], the QHP cannot terminate enrollment in the QHP in which the [qualified individual] newly enrolled based on failure to pay for any previously owed and unpaid premium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated in the Federally Facilitated Marketplace Enrollment Operational Policy & Guidance (CMS, Oct. 3, 2013). Means an enrollee who re-enrolls in the same plan cannot be re-terminated for prior unpaid premiums associated with the prior enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-month grace period for enrollees receiving APTC
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 156.270(d) requires issuers to observe a 3-consecutive month grace period before terminating coverage for those enrollees who when failing to timely pay their premiums are receiving APTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coupled with §155.430(d)(4) which sets the last day of enrollment when terminated after the grace period as the last day of the first month of the grace period. Consequently, individuals terminated at the conclusion of a grace period would owe at most 1 month of premiums net of any APTC paid on their behalf; individuals who attempt to enroll in new coverage while in a grace period (and whose coverage has not yet been terminated) could owe up to 3 months of premium, net of any APTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of grace periods spanning two plan years (attribution of payments)
rubrics_metrics.description: For individuals whose grace period for non-payment of premiums extends past the end of the annual OEP and who either auto-renews or makes an active plan selection that is a continuation of the same coverage, the issuer may attribute enrollee payments to the oldest outstanding debt in the existing grace period for the current coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced in the FFE Enrollment Manual, Section 6.3 (version effective Aug. 19, 2024). This guides how issuers allocate payments when a grace period straddles plan years and the enrollee continues the same coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuer notice requirement for premium delinquency
rubrics_metrics.description: Per §156.270(f), if an enrollee is delinquent on premium payment, the QHP issuer must provide the enrollee with notice of such payment delinquency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers offering QHPs in Exchanges on the Federal platform must provide such notices promptly and without undue delay, within 10 business days of the date the issuer should have discovered the delinquency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuers' nondiscrimination obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers may also have obligations under other applicable Federal laws prohibiting discrimination, and issuers are responsible for ensuring compliance with all applicable laws and regulations. There may also be separate, independent non-discrimination obligations under State law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reminder that marketplace-specific rules do not supplant other federal or state nondiscrimination duties; issuers must ensure compliance across legal regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and application of preponderance of the evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Preponderance of the evidence means 'proof by evidence that, compared with evidence opposing it, leads to the conclusion that the fact at issue is more likely true than not' (42 CFR 93.228; similar definitions at 45 CFR 412.001 and 45 CFR 1641.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites legal authorities and judicial interpretation (INS v. Cardoza‑Fonseca) clarifying that 'more likely than not' is greater than 50% probability; useful for administrative determinations and enforcement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of additional enforcement actions under 45 CFR 155.220(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS acknowledges that there are additional enforcement actions under 45 CFR 155.220(g) that are not addressed by this proposal and is considering future rulemaking to implement additional regulation changes to strengthen oversight and program integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals potential future expansion of enforcement frameworks; current rulemaking does not exhaust all enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on indefinite continuation of APTC through auto re-enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing procedures under §155.335 prohibit the indefinite continuation of APTC through auto re-enrollment in various circumstances, including for tax filers who do not comply with the failure to file and reconcile rules or whose authorization for the Exchange to obtain tax data from the IRS has expired (which is limited to 5 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auto re-enrollment cannot be used to perpetually continue APTC where statutory or procedural prerequisites (filing/reconciliation, IRS authorization) are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrollment special enrollment verification (SEP) scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, §155.420(g) provides that Exchanges on the Federal platform will conduct pre-enrollment special enrollment verification of eligibility only for special enrollment periods for loss of minimum essential coverage. Prior to the 2023 Payment Notice, Exchanges conducted manual verification for five SEPs: marriage, adoption, moving to a new coverage area, loss of minimum essential coverage, and Medicaid/CHIP denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes which SEPs are subject to pre-enrollment verification on the Federal platform and notes historical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and mechanism for SEP length descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions and information on the length of SEPs can be found at 45 CFR 155.420(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs readers where to find regulatory listings of SEP durations; useful for Exchanges and assisters implementing SEP determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'insurance affordability program'
rubrics_metrics.description: See the definition of 'insurance affordability program' at 45 CFR 155.300(a) and 42 CFR 435.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to regulatory definitions that determine eligibility and program application for Medicaid/CHIP and Marketplace subsidies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Health Benefits (EHB) categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1302(b)(1) of the ACA delineates the 10 general categories of EHB: ambulatory patient services; emergency services; hospitalization; maternity and newborn care; mental health and substance use disorder services, including behavioral health treatment; prescription drugs; rehabilitative and habilitative services and devices; laboratory services; preventive and wellness services and chronic disease management; and pediatric services, including oral and vision care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authoritative list used to determine benefit coverage baselines for QHPs and EHB benchmark plan construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: State variation in EHB-benchmark coverage for sex-trait modification
rubrics_metrics.description: The EHB-benchmark plans for California, Colorado, New Mexico, Vermont, and Washington specifically include coverage of some sex-trait modification; six other States' benchmarks do not expressly include or exclude such coverage; 40 States include language that excludes coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that EHB-benchmark plan design can vary by State and may include/exclude services like sex-trait modification—relevant for benefit determinations and disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicaid payer-of-last-resort requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by section 1902(a)(25) of the Social Security Act, Medicaid is the payer of last resort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory constraint on coverage/payment coordination relevant when individuals have multiple potential sources of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on issuer and Exchange responsibilities regarding unauthorized enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS reported a significant number of complaints of unauthorized enrollments and suspensions of agents/brokers for reasonable suspicion of fraudulent or abusive conduct related to unauthorized enrollments or plan switches; CMS has announced measures to prevent unauthorized agent and broker activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational and enforcement focus: issuers, Exchanges, and oversight must address unauthorized enrollments and agent/broker misconduct; CMS provides updates and actions (e.g., suspensions, policy changes) as guidance for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of APTC allocation and potential tax liability from auto re-enrollment/default plan selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollees auto re-enrolled from a bronze to a silver QHP under §155.335(j)(4) could incur unexpected tax liability if their APTC amount was determined based on inaccurate household income for the future year; an enrollee in bronze coverage who does not need to use the entire amount of the APTC has some protection; switching to a higher-premium plan could increase tax liability upon filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges and assisters should consider and communicate potential tax consequences of default or auto plan selections and how APTC application to different metal levels affects end-of-year reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDGE limited data set availability and request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The EDGE limited data set contains certain masked enrollment and claims data for on- and off-Exchange enrollees in risk adjustment covered plans and is derived from data collected for the HHS-operated risk adjustment program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request the EDGE limited data set, refer to the instructions provided on the CMS EDGE LDS files page; procedural requirement for researchers/analysts seeking enrollee-level data.
